messages.subject: Three-way Anova
parts:
Has anyone ever performed a three-way Anova in R? Is there a specific package I can use? I've been looking for a script, but can only find one for two-way at most. 

Thank you!
Susan

messages.author: 8d1674b7b16af1b1
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Three-way Anova
parts:
Does this do what you want? If not, could you 

model = lm(response ~ factor.1 + factor.2 + factor.3)
anova(model) 

If not, could you be more specific about what you're looking for?

Dave

messages.author: 8d1674b7b16af1b1
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Three-way Anova
parts:
The easiest thing would be a data.frame with four columns (three for your factors and one for your response).  You could make the table in Excel.  The best approach then is probably to export it from Excel as a csv ("comma-separated values") file and then import it into R with the read.csv function, which will automatically make the data.frame for you.

Hope this helps!

Dave
